title: Reverse-engineering the Intel 8087's tangent algorithm: more than CORDIC
summary: Ken Shirriff reverse-engineers the Intel 8087 floating-point coprocessor's microcode to analyze how it implements the tangent function, discovering that Intel used a sophisticated hybrid approach combining CORDIC with polynomial approximations rather than pure CORDIC, which was previously assumed.
problem_solved: Reveals the undocumented implementation details of how Intel optimized the tangent calculation in the 8087's hardware microcode.
why_valuable: Provides rare insight into Intel's engineering decisions from 1980, showing how they optimized performance by combining algorithms in ways that weren't documented in official specifications.
